outcome: self-efficacy (expected outcomes, expected self-efficacy, sources of self-efficacy)
cohort: 60 nulliparous pregnant women between 29 and 34 weeks of gestation who had not yet chosen their method of delivery were randomly assigned to intervention and control groups.
finding: Cognitive-behavioral group counseling significantly increased self-efficacy and the choice of normal vaginal delivery in the intervention group compared to the control group, reducing fear and anxiety.
mod_finding: 76.6% of mothers in the intervention group chose a normal vaginal delivery, with the conclusion suggesting this can reduce the amount of selective caesarean section.
